title.narrative: SO3. To contribute to nationallevel policy recommendations and legislative reforms in relation to child abuse cases, such as judicial interpretations and legislation amendments.

description.narrative: Improved judicial policy documents agreed amongst law enforcement agencies (SPC, SPP, MPS, MoJ, MSS), taking note of suggestions and leading to clearer, fairer and specialised case handling rules and practices and increased lawyer and social worker coverage in CSAs

title.narrative: SO 3.1 Number of substantive or procedural changes stemming from the Action included in National legal organs strategies, policy/legislative plans and guiding cases

description.narrative: SO 3.1 Number of substantive or procedural changes stemming from the Action included in National legal organs strategies, policy/legislative plans and guiding cases

comment.narrative: One piece of legal framework exists to date entitled The opinion concerning the offence of sexually abuse of juveniles. This focuses solely on substantive aspects of the law with no mention to procedure.The SPP has published in total six guiding cases on CSA crimes in November 2018 and July 2019 respectively to guide practitioners practice on dealing with CSA cases.

National judicial interpretation and local pilot rules. By 2023 improved judicial policy documents agreed amongst law enforcement agencies SPC SPP MPS MoJ MSS taking note of suggestions and leading to clearer fairer and specialised case handling rules and practices and increased lawyer and social worker coverage in CSAs. Major breakthrough was made in 2023 after the pandemic. Such as introduction of two national policies and SPP published three CSA Guiding Cases. More progress will be reported in the final report.
Pilot in three locations are underway. High level government involved Supreme Peoples Court National Peoples Congress.

title.narrative: R1. title.narrative: Indicator R1.2 Percentage of pilot prosecutors, police officers, justice social workers and legal aid lawyers demonstrate enhanced capacity to deal with CSA cases as a result of the Actions activities (reference guide etc.)

description.narrative: Indicator R1.2 Percentage of pilot prosecutors, police officers, justice social workers and legal aid lawyers demonstrate enhanced capacity to deal with CSA cases as a result of the Actions activities (reference guide etc.)

comment.narrative: Police officers use traditional interrogation methods to interview CSA victims which are not suitable for vulnerable underage children. Prosecutors legal aid lawyers and justice social workers do not have specialised skills.

By 2023 80 Action activity participants declare increased confidence and competency to deal with CSA as a result of the Actions interventions Between 20202023 CCLS research monitoring visits and research comparing of number of successful pilot cases with baseline confirm increase in the quality of police and prosecutors interviewing skills lawyers legal advice social workers support.

title.narrative: Indicator R1.1 Pilot prosecutors, police officers, justice social workers and legal aid lawyers demonstrate improved knowledge on genderbased violence and sexual violence, as well as safeguard obligations to children in the criminal justice system as a result of the Actions activities (online and offline)

description.narrative: Indicator R1.1 Pilot prosecutors, police officers, justice social workers and legal aid lawyers demonstrate improved knowledge on genderbased violence and sexual violence, as well as safeguard obligations to children in the criminal justice system as a result of the Actions activities (online and offline)

comment.narrative: There is very limited understanding on concepts such as genderbased violence and sexual violence particularly among police officers.Very few justice social workers and legal aid lawyers have reported that they are confident in supporting child victims justice social workers particularly expressed their lack of professional training opportunities.

Prosecutor category include both police officers and persecutors Court staff category refers to justice social workers.Between 2020 and 2023 At least 75 questionnairegroup exercise pass rate among Action participants indicate increased knowledge of childrens rights.The Action targets 90 people directly through offline activities both from the three pilot areas and other cities and collects feedback on the usefulness of materials in recipients daily work. Specific targets 50 from pilot areas 30 practitioners and 20 legal providers 70 female 40 from other areas 25 practitioners and 15 legal providers 70 female.Between 2020 and 2023Sharing of online awareness raising activities monitoring exceeds dissemination plan targets.
Much more training and coaching in the pilot areas is foreseen.

title.narrative: SO2: To improve coordination mechanisms between Chinese criminal justice practitioners, legal aid lawyers and justice social workers, to work effectively and sensitively with boy/girl victims and male/female suspects/defendants in criminal proceedings.

description.narrative: SO2: To improve coordination mechanisms between Chinese criminal justice practitioners, legal aid lawyers and justice social workers, to work effectively and sensitively with boy/girl victims and male/female suspects/defendants in criminal proceedings.

title.narrative: SO2.1 Procuratorateled multiagency response mechanisms and for dealing child sexual abuse cases to be put in place, leading to more effective and sensitive handling of CSA cases.

description.narrative: SO2.1 Procuratorateled multiagency response mechanisms and for dealing child sexual abuse cases to be put in place, leading to more effective and sensitive handling of CSA cases.

comment.narrative: Although some local procuratorates Ningbo and Kunming have introduced onestop forensic centres to support children in criminal justice proceedings the majority have no such mechanism and only limited information on awareness and capacity training is available for practitioners.Under current practice victims communicate to police officers with the presence of prosecutors or prosecutors interview victims separately. There is limited space for legal aid lawyers and justice social workers to intervene.

By 2023 at least 5 local Procuratorates take up championing child protection work within the local criminal justice system leading to Legal aid lawyers and justice social workers to support boygirl victims in CSA cases obtain more case information from early stage of proceedings Justice social workers to be able to support boygirl victims from first police interview. Increase the weight of the victim statements carry in CSA cases and courts deem such evidence as admissible.he experience sharing workshop was delivered in July 2023 and we undertook monitoring visits to Kunming and Ningbo pilot in 2023. More progress will be reported in the final report.
Good progress in very sensitive field of work judicial management of child sexual abuse. China is interested and open to Western best practice.
